message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to say "See you next year!" to my teacher R who is getting let go. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, Teacher R was new this year. He came in and tried to impose his own teaching and grading methods, which were very different from what we, the students, had ever experienced. It seems like he was pretty rigid about things, expecting us to do things his way even when it was clear that his methods were flawed. People pointed out his mistakes, but he still insisted on using his approach. That sounds frustrating for the students. He also took off points for scratch work that he didn't like and tried to deduct as many points as possible on tests, quizzes, and homework. Every student he had was subjected to this, without exception. That sounds really harsh and unfair. It's one thing to have strict grading, but another to be actively trying to take off points just because of personal preferences. Additionally, Teacher R took forever to grade assignments. We took a test the week before spring break and didn't get it back for about six weeks. He also refused to go over it with anyone, which is really unhelpful for students trying to understand their mistakes and improve. On top of that, he never offered help outside of the classroom and was hostile whenever asked for extra help. That makes it even harder for students to get the support they need. The administration noticed these issues, and we were informed that R wouldn't be coming back next year. It's no surprise that we were all overjoyed about this news. After the announcement, R completely checked out. He just wrote notes on the board, barely talked during class, and even went to Disneyland instead of attending one of the review days for exams. It seems like he lost motivation and stopped putting effort into his job. Yesterday, as I was walking out of R's classroom for the last time, I called out, "See you next year!" over my shoulder. My friends told me I'm the asshole for this, but I don't think so. I'm trying to figure out if I was right or wrong to say that. So, why did I say that? Maybe I was trying to get a reaction from him, or perhaps I was being sarcastic because we all knew he wasn't coming back. It could also be that I was expressing my own feelings about the situation, maybe even a bit of defiance or frustration. But my friends think it's wrong, so I need to consider their perspective. From their point of view, maybe they think it's mean or disrespectful to say something like that, especially when the teacher is already struggling and has checked out. They might feel that it's not kind to remind him that he's being let go, especially in such a public manner. They could also be concerned that it might have made the situation worse or caused unnecessary tension. On the other hand, I might feel that since he was being unfair and hostile towards us, it's justified to express some frustration. I might think that it's okay to have a bit of a parting shot, especially since he wasn't treating us well either. But I also need to consider whether this was the best way to handle the situation or if there was a more mature or kind way to express my feelings. I also need to think about the impact of my words. Did saying "See you next year!" have any real effect on Teacher R? Did it make the situation better or worse? If he was already checked out, maybe it didn't make much difference, but it's still important to consider how my actions affect others, even if they are difficult people. Another angle to consider is the concept of respect in the teacher-student relationship. Even if a teacher is not performing well or is being difficult, there's still an expectation of respect. Saying something like "See you next year!" might be seen as disrespectful, especially if it's said in a sarcastic or mocking tone. It could reinforce negative feelings or make the situation more uncomfortable for everyone involved. I also need to reflect on my own feelings. Why did I feel the need to say that? Was it because I was upset about how he treated us, or was it something else? Understanding my own motivations can help me determine whether my actions were appropriate or if I was acting out of anger or frustration. Furthermore, I should consider alternative ways to handle the situation. Instead of making a comment, maybe I could have talked to the teacher privately or expressed my concerns through the proper channels, like the administration. That might have been a more constructive way to address the issues without resorting to sarcasm or parting shots. In summary, while I might feel justified in expressing my frustration with Teacher R, the way I chose to do it by saying "See you next year!" could be seen as disrespectful or mean-spirited. It's important to consider the impact of my words on others and whether there's a more mature or constructive way to handle the situation. Reflecting on my own feelings and motivations can also help me understand why I acted the way I did and whether it was the best approach.
